fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD says, "Behold, I will stir up against Babylon and against the people of Leb-kamai the spirit of a destroyer." (Jeremiah 51:1) Not a famine and not a plague, but a destroyer. The target and the destroyer are both right there in the verse.

I get why a famine comes to mind, friend. But this verse says something different: the LORD will stir up "…the spirit of a destroyer." against Babylon and the people of Leb-kamai. (Jeremiah 51:1) It's an army-sized word, not a pantry-sized one.

A plague on cattle is a fair guess, friend. But here the LORD says He will stir up "…the spirit of a destroyer." against Babylon and the people of Leb-kamai. (Jeremiah 51:1) No cows in this verse, just the destroyer.

False is right, friend. The LORD says Israel and Judah "…have not been abandoned by their God, the LORD of Hosts, though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel." (Jeremiah 51:5) Both things are in the same verse. The guilt is named, and so is the LORD not abandoning them.

That's it, baker. The call says, "Flee from Babylon! Escape with your lives! Do not be destroyed in her punishment. For this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance; He will pay her what she deserves." (Jeremiah 51:6) The reason is right there in the verse.

That would be a quick way to clear a city, baker. But the verse never mentions a king giving an order. The reason it gives is, "…this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance; He will pay her what she deserves." (Jeremiah 51:6)

Drunk, yes, baker. "Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD, making the whole earth drunk." (Jeremiah 51:7) It's a picture, not a recipe. Then the verse says, "The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations have gone mad."

If only, friend. That's not what the verse says. Babylon was "…a gold cup in the hand of the LORD, making the whole earth drunk." and "…the nations have gone mad." (Jeremiah 51:7) The cup brings madness, not wisdom.

Yes, baker. The call says, "The LORD has brought forth our vindication; come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has accomplished." (Jeremiah 51:10) The telling is about what the LORD did. It's good news to share.

A getaway report would be juicy, baker, but the verse doesn't have one. It says, "come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has accomplished." (Jeremiah 51:10) The call is to tell what the LORD did.

That's right, baker. "The LORD has aroused the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because His plan is aimed at Babylon to destroy her…" (Jeremiah 51:11) The LORD stirs the kings of the Medes for this plan. The reason is stated right in the verse.
Egypt is a fun guess, friend, but it isn't in this verse. The verse says, "…His plan is aimed at Babylon to destroy her…" (Jeremiah 51:11) The Medes are stirred up for Babylon.
True, baker. "…the LORD has both devised and accomplished what He spoke against the people of Babylon." (Jeremiah 51:12) Planned and carried out, both in one verse. What He spoke is what He did.

Paint would be a funny thing to be missing, friend. But the verse says, "…his molten images are a fraud, and there is no breath in them." (Jeremiah 51:17) The passage names breath as what they lack, not paint.

That's right, baker. "They are worthless, a work to be mocked. In the time of their punishment they will perish." (Jeremiah 51:18) The verse calls the idols worthless. Then it says what happens to them: they perish.

Carried off sounds like what happens to treasure, friend, but the verse says something else. "In the time of their punishment they will perish." (Jeremiah 51:18) Nothing about hauling them away is mentioned. The word is perish.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "Before your very eyes I will repay Babylon and all the dwellers of Chaldea for all the evil they have done in Zion…" (Jeremiah 51:24) The reason is stated right there. The verse names where the evil was done: Zion.

Gold is a fun guess, friend, but Egypt isn't in this verse. The LORD says He will repay Babylon and the dwellers of Chaldea "…for all the evil they have done in Zion…" (Jeremiah 51:24) The verse says the evil was done in Zion.
Towers are a fun guess, baker, but they aren't in this verse. The LORD will repay them "…for all the evil they have done in Zion…" (Jeremiah 51:24) The reason given is the evil done in Zion.

I see why you might think so, baker. Stones from old buildings get reused all the time. But the LORD says, "No one shall retrieve from you a cornerstone or a foundation stone, because you will become desolate forever…" (Jeremiah 51:26) Not a cornerstone or a foundation stone gets retrieved.
